FFatTiger/coc-autopilot.description: Clash of Clans village automation: scheduled resource collection, worker checks, budget-based automatic upgrades, and an inspection dashboard. It operates a real device and does not touch the game process.
FFatTiger/coc-autopilot.body:
# Clash of Clans Autopilot

Village automation for Clash of Clans: scheduled resource collection, checking workers and Victory Stars, budget-based automatic upgrades, and a dashboard that shows status, browses history, and compares before/after screenshots.

It operates a real device: actions use ordinary tap injection, with no process injection, no modification of game data, and no calls to game APIs.
Numbers can be read through either of two switchable paths: the **OCR backend** (default; screenshots and recognition, no root required) and the **memory backend** (root reads `/proc/<pid>/mem`, bit-exact, and self-heals when addresses become invalid). See "[Two backends](#两种后端ocr-与内存)".

| | |
|---|---|
|  |  |
| The view after entering the village. The account info in the top-left corner is blurred | Dashboard home |

Before-and-after comparison of one inspection round. On the right you can see that the bubbles were tapped and resources went up:

## What it does

- **Collect resources**: recognize gold, elixir, and dark elixir bubbles in the village, tap each one to collect it, and automatically skip any that aren't full
- **Inspection**: read the three resources in the top-right, the worker count `在用/总数` (in use / total) in the bottom-right, and Victory Stars in the bottom-left
- **Auto upgrade**: open "Build" in the bottom-right, then the "Buildings and Heroes" list. Read the name, cost, and resource type of each upgradeable item, pick one that fits the budget to upgrade, and verify the result using the deducted amount
- **Auto research** (memory backend): tap Laboratory, then "Research", and page through all troops and spells (both elixir and dark elixir sets). Pick one that is affordable and under the cap to upgrade. The laboratory has only 1 slot, so it skips automatically while research is in progress, and it never uses gems to speed things up
- **Dashboard**: view the current status in the browser, the per-round earnings trend, and the history. Click any entry to see before-and-after screenshots, and drag the divider to compare them
- **Settings**: on the page, change the inspection schedule, toggle collection and upgrades, restrict which resource types may be spent (gold / elixir / dark elixir), and set **per-currency** single-spend caps
- **Manual trigger**: click a button to run a round immediately, with live progress and logs

## Risk Warning

**This may violate Supercell's Terms of Service.** The game prohibits automating play with third-party tools, and detection may lead to an account ban. The author is not responsible for any account losses.

This project deliberately avoids two kinds of approaches:

- It does **not write** game memory and does not inject into processes (there is anti-cheat, and writing memory is almost always detected)
- It does not call game protocol interfaces (resources are decided by the server, so changing them has no effect anyway)

The default OCR backend does only one thing: it uses `adb` to capture screenshots, uses OCR and template matching to understand the screen, and then uses touch injection to press buttons. From the server's point of view, this is just a very fast ordinary player.

The optional memory backend **reads only** the game process memory (`/proc/<pid>/mem`) to pin down resource numbers and upgrade costs precisely. It reads counters the game itself computes and writes nothing. It is more accurate than OCR, but leaves a heavier automation footprint and requires a rooted phone. Whether to enable it is your call.

RestRegular/dsh-memory.description: DSH Memory System: local-first memory — JSONL + local embeddings, five tools, auto recall, hard rules, visual panel.
RestRegular/dsh-memory.body:
# Memory System

**Local-first long-term memory that keeps every conversation connected.**

JSONL on disk · local vector retrieval · seven model tools · auto recall · hard rules · scope-based archiving · active suppression · visual management panel

[npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@restregular/dsh-memory) · [Issue tracker](https://github.com/RestRegular/dsh-memory/issues) · [Changelog](https://github.com/RestRegular/dsh-memory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

> **It doesn't just store a piece of text. It makes the model remember when it should, and use what it remembers when it's needed.**
> Memories stay on the local machine by default. It works without a vector service: retrieval automatically falls back to lexical matching and makes no network requests.

## What it solves

| Common problem | How the memory system handles it |
| --- | --- |
| A new session starts from zero, and switching windows loses last time's conclusions | Conclusions are saved as memories. A new session first injects a summary, then recalls by question on every turn |
| The same pitfall gets hit repeatedly, and a command looked up last time has to be looked up again | Behaviors such as publishing, deploying, or tool failures trigger targeted recall, and known solutions are reused directly |
| Rules are written but never enforced, and old sessions don't know about rules that were changed | `kind: rule` goes into a persistent section of the system prompt; adding or editing one issues a reminder |
| Temporary state gets treated as permanent fact | `kind: state` has a default 7-day TTL and a 'verify before use' prefix. After expiry it is hidden by default but never deleted automatically |
| Cloud memory is out of your control, so sensitive content can't be written | Everything is stored locally as JSONL; writes are scanned for credentials first; retrieval makes no network calls by default |

It also isn't 'dumping the whole chat log into the model.' Each memory is a self-contained statement, managed by scope, type, and importance. Recall has a token budget and deduplication. Outdated conclusions can be corrected by annotating them with `supersedes`, and the superseded versions no longer take part in retrieval, summarization, or recall by default (history remains accessible via `memory_get` and the panel), rather than being silently overwritten.

VaderChen/AppleJuice.body:
# AppleJuice

[Traditional Chinese](https://github.com/VaderChen/AppleJuice/blob/HEAD/README.md) · [English](https://github.com/VaderChen/AppleJuice/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Japanese](https://github.com/VaderChen/AppleJuice/blob/HEAD/README.ja.md) · [Korean](https://github.com/VaderChen/AppleJuice/blob/HEAD/README.ko.md)

A compatibility project for running Windows programs on Apple Silicon Macs, including the **Win64 Launcher** graphical launcher and the **x64arm** command-line program. AppleJuice provides PE/DLL loading and Windows compatibility services, and connects windows, graphics, audio, and input to native macOS interfaces and Metal.

The minimum system for release builds is **Apple Silicon, macOS 13.0**. Frame interpolation additionally requires **macOS 26 or later** and a supported device; when this condition is not met, interpolation is disabled. Normal program execution, MetalFX upscaling, and spatial audio mixing do not require an upgrade to macOS 27.

The repository includes the complete `x64kernel/` static SDK; normal builds do not require kernel source. The kernel is additionally provided by AppleJuiceKernel. Executables and Launcher packages after static linking are within the publishable scope of AppleJuice; when distributing them, the applicable license must be retained.

Currently maintains the single-core and multi-core execution paths for resident AOT. **The LLVM execution backend and the legacy JIT have been removed.** `--backend jit` is an existing interface name; resident AOT is still selected by default.

## Project Goals and Features

- **No Windows system files required**: The goal is to run supported programs without installing Windows or providing Windows system DLLs. The application and its bundled dependencies are supplied by the user.
- **Prefers native ARM64 instructions**: While maintaining x86/x64 instruction semantics and correct program behavior, use Apple Silicon native ARM64 and NEON vector operations wherever possible.
- **Uses native hardware acceleration**: Graphics and GPU computation prefer Metal; workloads such as video use macOS native frameworks and available hardware acceleration wherever possible.

aaazha686-oss/ktown4u-fansign-tracker.description: Ktown4u Signing Event Real-Time Sales Cloud Tracker (GitHub Actions)
aaazha686-oss/ktown4u-fansign-tracker.body:
# Ktown4u Cloud Auto-Scraper (GitHub Actions)

Let GitHub scrape Ktown4u signing-event sales automatically in the cloud, 24 hours a day, and store the data in the repository.
Your computer can be offline. When you have internet access, open the repository to view or download all historical data.

## File structure (place as-is in the repository)
```
your-repo/
├─ .github/workflows/track.yml   # Scheduled job (every 5 minutes)
├─ ktown4u_ci.py                 # Scraping script
├─ track_config.json             # Config: which events to track
└─ data/                         # Auto-generated: track_<event-no>.csv
```

## One-time setup (about 5 minutes)

1. **Create a GitHub repository** and select **Public**.
   > Why public: Actions in public repositories are **free and unlimited**. Private repositories get only 2000 minutes per month, which won't last long.
   > Signing-event sales figures are not sensitive data, so making the repository public is fine.

2. **Upload these three files** (keep the directory structure above): `.github/workflows/track.yml`, `ktown4u_ci.py`, `track_config.json`.
   - Web UI: Repository page → Add file → Upload files, then drag in the contents of the `cloud/` folder
     (don't drop the `.github/workflows/track.yml` directory level).

3. Open the **Actions** tab. If prompted, click **"I understand my workflows, enable them"** to enable them.

4. **Enter the event numbers you want to track**: edit the `events` field in `track_config.json`, for example:
   ```json
   { "shopNo": 164, "interval": 10, "burstSeconds": 200, "events": [44469917, 44468447] }
   ```
   - To get event numbers, use "Load current event / Search" in the local web app `ktown4u_app.py`.
   - After you commit and save, the next run starts tracking these events.

Done! From then on, it **runs automatically every 5 minutes**. Within each run, it scrapes every 10 seconds. Data is continuously appended to
`data/track_<event-no>.csv` (columns: `time, member, sales, delta`).

A cross-platform music player client. A single Flutter/Dart codebase natively supports **iOS / macOS / Windows / Linux / Android / HarmonyOS** on six platforms. The UI uses a dark glassmorphism and neon gradient design with a modern, futuristic feel. At build time, it automatically applies **packing and obfuscation** to prevent reverse engineering.

> This project was refactored from "Baiji Music Android Native v1.1.1". All C algorithm libraries (hash33 / zzc_sign / tripledes / qrc / qimei / comm) were ported to pure Dart. The network layer supports seven music sources: **QQ Music / NetEase Cloud Music / Kuwo Music / Kugou Music / Migu Music / JOOX / Soda Music**. Feature modules cover search, playback, playlists, downloads, QR code login, and local music.

---

## v2.6.3 Update Highlights (Official Release)

| Optimization | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ⚡ **Lyrics engine rewritten in-house** | Reverse-engineered BaiMusic 4.7's lyric rendering and rewrote `LiteLyricsView` in pure Dart + Canvas, replacing the `flutter_lyric` engine. The old engine ran `saveLayer` and glyph rasterization on every visible line each frame, so mid-range devices dropped frames during per-character sweeps. The new engine reads the playback position once per frame and computes the fill with BaiMusic-style linear interpolation. **Only the current line** redraws a single `clipRect` thin rectangle (no saveLayer, no per-frame allocations), and other lines are not redrawn at all. When the line changes, it smoothly `animateTo`s (140ms), and dragging pauses auto-follow |
| 🎨 **Appearance and interaction unchanged** | The three colors, font size, font weight, alignment, translations, and click-to-seek all carry over. The `computeFillOffset` linear sweep and per-character pixel interpolation, obtained through reverse engineering, keep transitions smooth without jitter |

## v2.6.2-fix2 Update Highlights (Revised Release)

| Optimization | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 🎵 **Lyrics scrolling stutter fix** | The progress source `changes` no longer forwards `onPositionChanged` every frame. Sampling twice, once there and once in the engine Ticker, caused per-frame rebuilds and cache clears, which produced frame drops and jumps. It now carries only play/stop and seek discrete events. Per-character highlighting is still sampled every frame by the engine Ticker, so it stays responsive and smooth |
| ✨ **Per-character sweep visual** | Turned off the per-character continuous floating from the appleMusic preset, which kept an idle Ticker spinning. The characters no longer move; only a clean per-character sweep remains, matching the effect of comparable software |

After downloading the `.dmg`, you need to remove the quarantine flag before opening the app for the first time, because it is not signed by Apple:

```bash
sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/WeaselVision.app
```

Extract `WeaselVision_0.5.0_Windows_<arch>.zip` and run `weasel-gpui.exe` directly (portable version, no installation required).

```bash
cd weasel_vision
```

wlrwx/football-engine.body:
# Sporttery Engine

Sporttery football probability analysis and virtual betting simulation system. It is based on the Dixon-Coles Poisson model and Monte Carlo simulation, uses market-dominant probability fusion, allocates virtual bets with the Kelly criterion, and runs fully automatically on GitHub Actions at zero server cost. **For data analysis and algorithm learning only. It does not constitute any betting advice. All outputs are virtual bookkeeping.**

## Core Principles (driven by data evidence from 2026-08)

1. **The market is the benchmark**: Across a 426-match ledger, the pure market (de-vigged) Brier score of 0.583 outperforms every model stream (0.646+). Fusion weight is therefore market-dominant (0.75), and models and third-party sources only make minor adjustments.
2. **Every switch is decided by data**: Each step of the fusion chain is a config switch (`config/prediction.json["fusion"]["post_fusion"]`). Whether each step stays is decided by paired replay of settled ledgers via `scripts/ablation_replay.py`.
3. **Self-evolution with guardrails**: Any automatic enabling of the calibration layer or LGBM must pass a time-based split and a paired significance test, and it is automatically disabled if performance degrades. See `docs/UPGRADE2_20260829.md`.

## Architecture

```
Daily loop: fetch data → fusion prediction (fusion.py, full trace) → lock → settle → self-learning
Weekly loop: backtest → weight optimization (champion/challenger) → parameter refit → Monday health check
Evolution loop: clean samples (chain=v2) accumulate → calibration layer auto re-enable/disable (calibration_auto)
                      → LGBM shadow training + validation (lgbm_shadow) → weekly effect evaluation (tracker)
```

## Tech Stack

- Python 3.12 / numpy / scikit-learn / LightGBM / joblib
- GitHub Actions (computation) + GitHub Pages (reports)
- No database. Pure CSV/JSON with git versioning. Ledgers are append-only.

# Waterfall · ICT.RUN Photography

Photography works site for ICT.RUN, online at **[p.zli.li](https://p.zli.li)**. The same works can be viewed in two ways:

- **GNOMON** (site homepage): a circular 3D gallery. Walking one loop takes you from early morning to late night, and the light in the corridor changes with the time.
- **Classic** ([/classic/](https://p.zli.li/classic/)): the original theme masonry waterfall layout, with an EXIF watermark tool. When a device can't handle 3D, it automatically falls back to this view.

| Early Morning | Nightfall |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

## GNOMON

> A day of light, in one loop.

GNOMON is the needle on a sundial that casts the shadow. The works are divided into five time periods based on the light in the picture (First Light, Rush Hour, High Noon, Golden Hour, Night Shift), hung along the outer and inner walls of the circular corridor.

- **Walk**: scroll, drag, or swipe on a touchscreen to move around; ← → switch time periods; the timeline at the bottom jumps directly to any period.
- **View**: click a photo and it is lifted off the wall and floats in front of you, with the corridor behind it blurred. Click again to see the full-size image.
- **Light**: the colors of the walls, floor, and fog interpolate with the time of day. After nightfall the page switches to dark. Each work has a spotlight, and its glow follows the size and proportions of the work.
- **Rendering**: ACES tone mapping, spotlight bloom, a faint sheen on the matte floor, and soft shadows at the wall corners. The works' own colors are preserved.
- **List**: switch to Index in the top bar to browse all works by time period.

Native JavaScript + [three.js](https://threejs.org/) r187 (loaded from a CDN), no build step required. For implementation details, data format, and file descriptions, see [gnomon/README.md](https://github.com/xuemian168/waterfall/blob/HEAD/gnomon/README.md).

### Low-Performance Fallback

[gnomon/js/fallback.js](https://github.com/xuemian168/waterfall/blob/HEAD/gnomon/js/fallback.js) runs first on the page:

1. Before loading: on devices without WebGL2, with software rendering, with data saver enabled, or with less than 4 GB of memory, the page jumps to `/classic/` before downloading three.js.
2. After entering the corridor: it measures the frame rate for 3 seconds. If it falls below 24 fps, a notice appears at the top, and you can switch to Classic or stay.

Adding `?classic` or `?gnomon` to the URL selects a view manually, and the choice is remembered in the browser.

## 🚀 Quick Start for Chinese Users (supplementary guide, not original content)

### What this is and what problem it solves

Open Code Review is an AI-driven code review CLI tool (the command name is `ocr`), originating from an AI code review assistant that Alibaba used internally for two years. It reads Git diffs, hands the changed files to a configurable LLM, and an agent with tool-calling capabilities produces structured review comments with line-level precision.
